newsitem.title: USA: CRP extension must be under new terms - Glickman.
newsitem.headline: CRP extension must be under new terms - Glickman.

text.p: Any extension of expiring contracts under the Conservation Reserve Program would have to be under the terms of the new program, Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Thursday.

Speaking to reporters after addressing a food policy conference, Glickman said he would prefer to see no extension of expiring CRP contracts this fall, but said that if there were, they would have to be under new contract terms.
"As a general proposition, I don't like extensions," Glickman said. But he added some farmers may need an extension of current contracts to make the best planting decisions.

House Agriculture Committee Chairman Bob Smith, Republican of Oregon, said earlier this week he would consider supporting a one-year extension of the CRP contracts set to expire this fall. Some 22 million acres worth of contracts mature by September.
Glickman said CRP signup is going "extremely well," and said farmers will be notified by late May or early June whether or not their acreage was accepted into the new program.

Glickman also defended the administration's proposal to offset the $65 million payment to crown Butte mines to not mine near Yellowstone National Park by delaying for one year enrollment of two million acres in the CRP.
"I don't look at this as affecting the (CRP) program at all," Glickman said.
He said that the decision to offset the cost of the package through the CRP plan was "a very difficult decision," but said that the USDA is committed to the full inclusion of acres into the CRP.
Under the plan, USDA will enroll 17 million acres of land into the CRP this year instead of the budgeted 19 million acres, and will enroll an extra two million acres the following year.
Farm groups and some lawmakers criticized the plan as being unfair to agriculture, and said its approval may face rough going on Capitol Hill.
